svg.title: Composite
svg.desc: Composite. Treat single objects and groups of objects through one interface, so a whole tree answers a question the way one leaf does. Step 1, Type checks everywhere: usage() asks File or Folder? at every node; each other walk does too, so a new kind edits all four. Step 2, One interface for both: File and Folder implement Node.size(): a file returns its own size, a folder sums its children's. Step 3, One call, the whole tree: project.size() runs down the tree and the sums come back up: icons 4, src 15, assets 52, project 71. Step 4, Uniform, with a catch: A Symlink leaf joins and Folder stays untouched. The catch: where add(child) lives, and no cycles.

g.text: usage() asks File or Folder? at every node; each other walk does too, so a new kind edits all four.
File and Folder implement Node.size(): a file returns its own size, a folder sums its children's.
project.size() runs down the tree and the sums come back up: icons 4, src 15, assets 52, project 71.
A Symlink leaf joins and Folder stays untouched. The catch: where add(child) lives, and no cycles.
A Folder calls size() on each child and never asks if it is a File or a Folder
Shown one level at a time; at runtime size() goes depth-first, one child after another
Transparency: add(child) on Node, so a File must refuse it
Safety: add(child) only on Folder, so clients need its type
No cycles: a folder can't be added inside itself or a subfolder
Real trees: the DOM (Node, Element), java.awt.Container, React, syntax trees
